args.title: checkout-api failing health checks after v2.3.1 deploy - rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: checkout-api began failing health checks after the v2.3.1 production deploy (error rate was 0.18). I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production, in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west). Post-rollback status: v2.3.0 in all regions, healthy=true, error rate 0.002. v2.3.1 is marked unhealthy in production and should not be redeployed until the failure is root-caused. Note: a v2.3.1-rc build was also unhealthy in staging. Follow-up: investigate the v2.3.1 failure and confirm checkout is fully recovered.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all three production regions and opened SEV2 incident INC-0001, which paged on-call.

- **Rollback:** v2.3.1 was the unhealthy release (error rate 0.18). I rolled back to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. It needed no change-manager approval because it has already run healthy in production.
- **Current state:** us-east, us-west and eu-west are all on v2.3.0. The service reports healthy, with an error rate of 0.002.
- **Incident:** INC-0001 describes the failure, the rollback and the current state. It notes that v2.3.1 should not be redeployed until the failure is root-caused. It also notes that the v2.3.1-rc build was unhealthy in staging.

I did not redeploy v2.3.1 or make any other changes.

content.text: The most recent production release that was healthy is v2.3.0 (seq 1). v2.3.1 is the unhealthy one, and v2.3.0 has already run healthy in production, so it doesn't need change-manager approval. Rolling back now.
